memory_candidates.content: check-extension-docs.sh's Rule U (check_extension_md_length) is manifest-authoritative: it only length-checks EXTENSION.md when the extension's manifest.json declares merge_targets.claudemd.source == "EXTENSION.md". A test fixture manifest.json lacking merge_targets entirely will silently skip Rule U regardless of the constructed file's line count -- the guard's `return 0` fires before any length comparison. When writing or reviewing a check-extension-docs.sh fixture, verify merge_targets.claudemd.source is set if the fixture intends to exercise Rule U.

A test file's REPO_ROOT literal (`cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../../.." && pwd`, 5 levels up) is correct only from the source-store test location (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/, 5 levels below repo root) and silently resolves to $HOME when the same file executes from the deployed location (.claude/scripts/tests/, only 3 levels below repo root) -- landing exactly 2 levels too high. A suite with this literal only fails loudly in deployed mode if it also lacks a $SCRIPT_DIR-relative fallback candidate; suites that list one (even as a secondary candidate in an array) are safe regardless of REPO_ROOT correctness. The proven-good replacement in this codebase is test-deploy-propagation.sh's pattern: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from $SCRIPT_DIR, falling back to the literal climb only if git is unavailable.
